A variant of object-aligned rendering where data is stored as a set of 2D texture slices.
Proxy polygons are simple rectangles aligned with slices.
To avoid data replication, slices can be reconstructed on the fly, incurring performance overhead.
*   **Time Complexity:** Rendering time is proportional to the number of slices and the resolution of the image.
*   **3D Textures:** $O(N)$ where $N$ is the number of voxels.
*   **When to Use:** Interactive visualization where performance is critical and artifacts are acceptable or mitigated (e.g., view-aligned slices).
*   **When Not to Use:** High-quality offline rendering requiring precise sampling (use ray casting); memory-constrained environments with large volumes using 2D textures.
Texture-Based Volume Rendering was developed to accelerate volume rendering on graphics hardware.
